text: With the Dockerfile, the Terraform, the pipeline, the AWS bucket, and the replication job all written, Theo runs terraform apply for the first time. Six resources come up together: resource group, VNet, subnet, ACR, the AKS cluster, and the storefront Helm release onto it.

A push to main triggers the pipeline end to end: build, test, scan, push to ACR, then an OIDC login to Azure and a helm upgrade --install against aks-driftwood-prod. Nobody touches kubectl by hand anywhere in the sequence.

kubectl get pods shows ten pods, all 1 of 1 Running -- exactly matching minReplicas 10 from Lesson 4's values-prod.yaml. The autoscaler brought the deployment straight to its configured floor, the way it's designed to.

Ten pods, more than we'll probably need this early, but better safe than sorry before launch, Theo notes, checking it off and moving to the smoke test. Both the rollout status check and the health endpoint come back clean. That night, the replication job runs its first unattended pass successfully.

Priya checks the single-point-of-failure problem is gone. Casey checks none of it needed a person at a keyboard. Ten running pods, zero manual steps, and a nightly backup landing in a second cloud reads like an unambiguous win -- and for now, it is one.
